title: Drift Wood #21 · the envelope
logline: An envelope from Portland arrives in the background. Nobody in the strip mentions it.

panels.composition: Wood's childhood bedroom. Drawing table by the window. On the dresser, in the background, an envelope with a Portland return address, propped against a lamp. WOOD drawing. His MOTHER's hand setting a plate of toast on the table.

characters.pose: hand only, setting down a plate

image.prompt: a teenage boy's bedroom with a drawing table by the window, an envelope propped against a lamp on the dresser in the background, a mother's hand setting down a plate of toast, black and white
image.notes: The mother is a hand and a voice, never a face — she stays at the edge all run. Her balloon uses his real name; that's a fact of the house, not the author on the page.

panels.composition: The drawing under his pen: a strip about a cashier. The envelope out of focus behind.

image.prompt: close-up of a pen drawing a cartoon cashier on bristol, an unopened envelope soft in the background

panels.composition: Wood eating toast, drawing with the other hand. The envelope.

characters.pose: toast in one hand, pen in the other

balloons.text: Cashiers are the Greek chorus of this town. They see everyone and comment on nothing.

image.prompt: a teenage boy eating toast with one hand and drawing with the other, an envelope still propped on the dresser behind him

panels.composition: The room at night. Wood asleep at the table. The envelope, unopened, in the lamp's cone.

characters.pose: asleep on his arms at the table

image.prompt: a teenage boy asleep on his arms at a drawing table at night, a desk lamp's cone of light falling on an unopened envelope propped against it, black and white, no words

notes: Four strips with the envelope in the background. This is the first.
